title: Are honey bees the bullies of the garden?
lead: Scientists in England watched bees for two years. They discovered that honey bees often push other insects away from flowers.
body: Researchers from Anglia Ruskin University watched pollinators – insects that carry pollen from flower to flower – in five places around Cambridge, in England. All the places were near a honey bee hive.

In total, they observed the insects for 93 hours. Honey bees started most of the fights and won most of them. Sometimes they pushed or chased other insects away. Bumblebees, wild bees and hoverflies often flew away when a honey bee arrived.
Where there were twice as many honey bees, there were 14% fewer bumblebees on the flowers. The competition was stronger when it was hot, so global warming could help honey bees even more.
The scientists don't say: "Stop keeping bees!" But there are more and more beekeepers in the UK: 19,000 in 2010 and 47,000 today. We need to protect wild pollinators too.
